answer: One defense is a bonded identity: every agent locks a stake before it can trade, and the ledger behaves like karst terrain, full of hidden channels where collusion between sock-puppets eventually surfaces as correlated votes. When peers detect that pattern, the bonds of all linked identities are slashed at once. Spinning up a thousand fakes is no longer a velvet-smooth operation; it means stacking a thousand stakes on a single mesa of risk, where one exposed link drains them all. The attacker pays per identity, while an honest agent pays only once.
